mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investments, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% in a quarter indicates a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3% in a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a supply shock, which increases input costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month, combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2%, signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month signals strong economic demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS increase > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% in a quarter, combined with an increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a month, signals stagflation, which increases costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decrease > 0.5% in 3 months and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where both conditions are met.
